operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are lowercase, no spaces; DDL uses double-quoted names and backtick-quoted `train` in route FK — sqlite accepts both, keep original DDL verbatim.
Tiny DB: train=11, station=11, route=18, weekly_weather=16 rows; no huge-table sampling needed, full read is fine.
All columns notnull=0 (nullable) despite being PKs; PKs are declared via table-level PRIMARY KEY, so pragma notnull=0 — do not treat as NOT NULL.
route and weekly_weather have composite PKs (train_id,station_id) and (station_id,day_of_week); composite-PK members get max_l0=30 per spec.
route.train_id FK -> train.id and route.station_id FK -> station.id; weekly_weather.station_id FK -> station.id; all parents exist and are unique (PK).
No self-references, no dangling FKs, no missing parents — clean FK graph: train, station at level 0; route, weekly_weather at level 1.
Declared types: INT (Number fuzzer), TEXT (String fuzzer), REAL (Number fuzzer, scale from no args -> default). No Date/Time/Bool/Bit dispatch.
train.time is TEXT storing 'HH:MM' (e.g. '17:15', '4:49', '06:30') — mixed zero-padding, NOT a declared time type, so TS String fuzzer will not produce time-like values.
train.interval has distinct=1 ('Daily') — String sampler with 1 element will mostly return 'Daily' plus contaminated variants.
weekly_weather.day_of_week TEXT with 7 distinct weekday names — String fuzzer, no enum awareness.
precipitation REAL values are round tens (90.0, 20.0, ...) — Number float fuzzer will perturb by ±0.01/±0.02, producing implausible decimals.
train_number INT values are 5-digit (16724, 16127) — Number fuzzer range is [-10^scale,10^scale] with default scale, likely far from 5-digit range.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on id/train_number/station_id/train_id: default scale (no args in INT) -> range roughly [-10^0..10^0]? Actually INT with no (a,b) -> scale default; values perturbed ±1/±2 — likely small ints, missing 5-digit train_number and 1..11 id ranges.

String fuzzer on name/origin/destination/network_name/services/local_authority: random charset strings + contamination, so joins on these text columns rarely match original values -> FN on equality predicates.
String fuzzer on train.time: produces random strings, not 'HH:MM' — queries comparing time strings will mostly fail to match -> FN.
String fuzzer on day_of_week: random strings, not weekday names — WHERE day_of_week='Monday' returns empty -> FN.
String fuzzer on interval (1 distinct): sampler with 1 element returns 'Daily' w.h.p. but contamination (0.5) corrupts it -> some FN.
Number fuzzer on high_temperature/low_temperature/wind_speed_mph: small ints, not 50-70 range -> range predicates (BETWEEN 50 AND 70) may return empty or wrong -> FN.
Number float fuzzer on precipitation: values near 0 with ±0.01 perturbation, not round tens -> equality/range on precipitation misses -> FN.

Composite PKs (route, weekly_weather): sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicate PK tuples; with small sizes and FK draws from small parent sets, many rows dropped -> small instances, possible empty tables -> FN.

FK child columns draw from parent's final values with replacement; parent id ranges are small ints from Number fuzzer, so route/weekly_weather get small int FKs — consistent but not matching original id semantics.
No NOT NULL/CHECK enforcement in Python; rows violating constraints skipped at insert — here all nullable so few skips, but PK duplicates filtered in Python.

Missing ties/duplicates: original has distinct counts < row counts (e.g. route.train_id 10 distinct in 18 rows, weekly_weather.station_id 5 in 16) — TS may produce fewer duplicates -> FP on COUNT(DISTINCT) or GROUP BY queries expecting ties.
No Date/Time declared types, so Date/Time fuzzers unused; train.time as TEXT means time-format queries rely on String fuzzer which won't match -> systematic FN on time predicates.
